questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: My best friend lives in the city i was going to exchange in. Other than that i am also fluent in German which made Munich an obvious destination to go on exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It wasnt too hard to get information regarding the univeristy, since i was assigned a 'buddy' who also spoke my native language (danish). He helped me out a ton with all the practical information regarding the university (What courses were available, How to pay semester fees, Where the different campuses are etc.)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had received occasional emails from the university on how i should prepare for my stay in Munich. There was also an introduction seminar for exchange students before the semester began.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty hard, but the University had made it clear that the housing market in Munich is pretty tough. i think i applied for about 50 rooms before i received an answer. I'd recommend other students to only apply for recently posted offers, and maybe choose an Area outside of the city to live. I lived all the way in Garching, but due to the ease of public transit in the city it only took about 30 mins to get to Uni. Direct transit is pretty nice and fast, so try to look for housing at the final destinations of the Train/Sub that stops at your Uni if you want a realistic oppurtunity for private housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Know how the public transportation system works in your city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some courses, that didnt even exist anymore, were still listed in the course catalogue. I emailed two profs who told me their courses had be discontinued, which drastically changed my original course plan. Some courses didnt even have course descriptions(and many were lacking), which made it very hard to tell what i should register for.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Online registration through the university portal.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Most help came from my university assigned 'buddy'. But there was also an Erasmus councillor for my faculty whom i could contact if i needed adminstrative help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was succesful in registering for all my classes. However, like i mentioned, some courses i wanted to take had been discontinued, despite still being on the course catalogue. In general course capacity was no problem.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware of the rules for your faculty, they can be kind of hidden. Nowhere, except for when i first applied through mobility online, did it state that i needed to take 60% of my courses from my faculty (Physics). Im glad i remembered that fact, else i wouldnt have been able to get my transcript.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Some courses were good, but some were severely lacking in structure and communication. Some teachers would upload solutions to every problem set and give a good overview of what would be taught throughout the course, while some didnt care at all and just seemed to 'wing' their courses, with no way to tell what would be taught from week to week (e.g. General Relativity). A very mixed bag for sure.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 15 ECTS Masters courses and 15 ECTS Bachelors courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think UCPH has a higher standard for what is expected of the teachers (Organization of course and clear communication to students especially.). But at my exchange institution i felt a lot more challenged(which was pretty refreshing actually), since there was a higher expectation to the amount of work you had to hand in every week.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
General Relativity, Stochastic dynamics - from Brownian motion to
fluctuating fields, Game Theory, Physics of the human body: biosignals and biosensors, Introduction to Machine Learning

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
All of the above courses were well organized and had pretty good professors. 

The one exception is General Relativity where i felt lost all the time. It was a terribly organized course and it was pretty much impossible to get individual help, since all the Exercise lessons were just a teacher presenting solutions to problems (which was always messy, since the tutors were usually ill prepared)

My advice is: Ask around about courses from local students before choosing.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to pay 85eur to be enrolled at the University for the semester.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Short term fitness memberships were a lot more expensive than expected. Look for local gyns with student discounts.

Groceries are pretty cheap in general.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a sports association at the Uni but i didnt participate.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just engage with locals. Go to bars and public events and talk to new people. Enjoy the freedom of living in a country where you dont know anyone yet.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the mountains. You can get around pretty much everywhere with the cheap 'Germany card' where you can use all German trains for a flat fee of 38 eur. Go for a hike somewhere outside the city. Or go watch a football game at a local pub.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, since my best friend lives there and i speak the language fluently. I hung out with his friend group often.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in language exchange events, those look pretty fun, i saw them hanging about a few times. You could also try starting at some sports at the uni sport association.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Theres a lot more emphasis on work culture in Germany. People are less outgoing and spend a lot more time on studying than i am used to. It was hard to get people to come out to the bar. German humor is also very different from Danish humor so my jokes didnt always land.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I adopted part of the german work culture and feel a lot more disciplined as a person, which i am pretty glad for.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: be aware that it is a much more common occurence that people fail courses at my host institution. It is not atypical for a couse to have an 80% fail rate. Do your research before picking and dont become overconfident when picking; You can easily be overwhelmed.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in a foreign country has made me feel much more at home in my own home country. When everything is suddenly new and confusing, its easy to feel out of place, but that just makes you appreciate the ease of being home that much more.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding accomodation for sure. I lived with my best friend for my first month just because it was THAT hard to find a room. I recommend looking well in advance for accomodation, and dont bet on the University providing you any (Even though they say its a 50/50 chance youll receive campus accomodation it its more like 30/70).

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
